original.target_description: Study 1 online experiment: consent to organ donation in opt-out versus opt-in default conditions; neutral third arm. Located on journal p.1338 (PDF p.1), rather than supplied p.2.

n.location: p.1338, Defaults and Organ Donations, first experiment
n.quote: 161 respondents were asked whether they would be donors on the basis of one of three questions with varying defaults.
n.sample_role: Respondents; 161 is the whole three-arm experiment. The analytic n for the opt-out versus opt-in comparison is not separately printed.
n.exclusions: Not documented in the main article.

es.location: p.1338, Defaults and Organ Donations, first-experiment results
es.quote: Revealed donation rates were about twice as high when opting-out as when opting-in.

p.location: p.1338, Defaults and Organ Donations, first-experiment results
p.quote: Only the opt-in condition, the current practice in the United States, was significantly lower.

replication.target_description: Part 1 direct replication, combined samples, opt-out versus opt-in organ-donation consent; chi-squared comparison reported with odds ratio. Temporary-choice extension excluded.

n.location: Table 5, Replication of Experiment 1, combined replication sample n
n.sample_role: Participants in the two compared direct-replication arms; printed arm counts, without calculating their sum.
n.exclusions: 91 participants excluded across the project for English proficiency, seriousness, hypothesis knowledge, completion and residence; Part 1 temporary-choice extension participants are outside this direct comparison.

es.location: Results, Part 1: Replication of Johnson and Goldstein (2003), first paragraph

p.location: Results, Part 1: Replication of Johnson and Goldstein (2003), first paragraph

reported_success.location: Summary of replication findings, first paragraph
reported_success.quote: We replicated the default effects from Johnson and Goldstein (2003).

notes: Original title verified against author-hosted PDF https://www.dangoldstein.com/papers/DefaultsScience.pdf (DOI landing returned 403; no retry). The supplied original page locator points to a different page; study 1 and the stated outcome identify the online experiment on p.1338. No numerical effect size, test statistic or p value for that original contrast is printed in the main article; no values are borrowed from the country analyses or from the replication authors’ reconstructed original data. Replication OR and p are from the same chi-squared comparison, not the regression intercept.
